name: ioctl_iflags
synopsis: int ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, void *arg);
description: Retrieves and modifies inode flags for files and directories on Linux filesystems. These flags alter file semantics and can be accessed using specific ioctl operations like FS_IOC_GETFLAGS and FS_IOC_SETFLAGS.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the file or directory to operate on

parameters.name: request
parameters.description: The ioctl request code, such as FS_IOC_GETFLAGS or FS_IOC_SETFLAGS

parameters.name: arg
parameters.description: Pointer to the argument, typically a pointer to an int for storing or retrieving flags

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and sets errno

errors.description: Operation not permitted, such as when the caller lacks necessary capabilities or ownership
Bad address, if the argument pointer is invalid
Invalid argument, if the request or flags are not supported

bugs: The argument for FS_IOC_GETFLAGS and FS_IOC_SETFLAGS is specified as int*, but the kernel source implies it should be long*, which may lead to inconsistencies.
versions: Linux, with some flags introduced as early as Linux 2.6.0 and others in later versions like 2.6.39.
